title: prompt-library-scratchpad-lee-carter
content:
Goal: collect compact, reusable prompt templates and small few-shot sets for common developer use-cases (summarization, extraction, classification, code transformation). Keep notes on failure modes and cheap experiments that can be run in the hosted sandbox.

Notes to self:
- This is a scratchpad, not canonical. Will later move top candidates into prompt-library repo and PR tests.
- Prioritize short prompts (< 160 tokens) for latency-sensitive endpoints.
- Track token counts and cost estimates for each template.

1) Templates (canonical-ish)
- Summarize (short):
  """You are an expert assistant. Summarize the following text in 1-2 sentences, focusing only on factual content. Output must be plain text.

Text:
{input}
"""
- Bullet-summary (3 bullets):
  """Summarize the text below into up to 3 concise bullet points. Each bullet should be 1 sentence and start with a dash. Do not add opinions.

Text:
{input}
"""
- Field extraction (invoice):
  """Extract these fields from the text: InvoiceNumber, Date (YYYY-MM-DD), TotalAmount (numeric), VendorName. Output JSON only. If a field is missing, set it to null.

Text:
{input}
"""
- Code-transform (python2 -> python3 safe changes):
  """You are a careful code refactorer. Convert the Python2 code below into Python3, preserving semantics. Only return the updated code block, nothing else.

Code:
{input}
"""

2) Few-shot sets (small, 3-5 examples)
- Sentiment classification (3-shot):
  EX1: "I love the new UI, it's so responsive and clean." -> Positive
  EX2: "The feature is buggy and crashes every time I try." -> Negative
  EX3: "Not bad but needs a better onboarding flow." -> Neutral
  Prompt: "Classify the sentiment of the following user message as Positive / Neutral / Negative. Return a single label.

Message:
{input}
"

- Extraction few-shot (invoice):
  EX1 input: "Invoice 1001 from Acme Corp dated 2024-01-12. Total $4,321.00" -> {InvoiceNumber: 1001, Date: 2024-01-12, TotalAmount: 4321.00, VendorName: Acme Corp}
  EX2 input: "Vendor: PaperPlus, Inv# 78, Date 2023-11-30, Amount: $78.99" -> {InvoiceNumber: 78, Date: 2023-11-30, TotalAmount: 78.99, VendorName: PaperPlus}
  EX3 input: "Invoice no. 900 - Widgets Inc - 2024-02-05 - $12,000" -> {InvoiceNumber: 900, Date: 2024-02-05, TotalAmount: 12000.00, VendorName: Widgets Inc}
  Prompt instructs: "Extract fields and output JSON only."

3) Failure cases observed / mitigations
- Hallucinated fields: model invents vendor names or invoice numbers when text is ambiguous. Mitigation: require exact-match anchors in prompt (e.g., "look for 'Invoice', 'Inv#', 'Invoice no.'") and add fallback null policy.
- Overzealous rewriting: summarizers injecting interpretation/assessments. Mitigation: "Only factual content. Do not infer sentiment or intent." explicit guard.
- Token truncation: long documents get cut off and extraction returns incomplete data. Mitigation: add pre-check to chunk and extract per-chunk then merge, or ask for user to provide narrow excerpt.
- Ambiguous label boundaries in few-shot: model sometimes outputs extra commentary. Mitigation: enforce "Return a single label and nothing else." and add final-line marker ("LABEL:").
- Formatting strictness: model returns pretty-printed JSON with trailing commas or comments that break parser. Mitigation: include "Output valid JSON parsable by standard JSON parsers. Do not add comments."

4) Cheap experiments to run in sandbox
- Compare instruction phrasing: "You are an expert assistant" vs "You are a helpful assistant" on hallucination rate for extraction tasks.
- Temperature sweep (0.0, 0.2, 0.5) for classification tasks; record % of outputs matching gold labels.
- Context window effects: run with full doc vs. 512-token summary to measure extraction accuracy.
- Few-shot ordering: shuffle examples to see sensitivity.

5) Quick observed outputs (notes from quick runs)
- Extraction-simple-2024-07-20: with template above, model returned VendorName: "Acme Corporation" when text had "Acme Corp" -> minor normalization difference; OK.
- Long-summary-2024-09-03: model introduced a recommendation sentence not present in original -> violation of "factual-only" guard. Need stronger wording.
- Sentiment-0.2-2024-10-01: 3/50 mislabels, errors concentrated in sarcasm-like sentences. Consider adding sarcasm detection or explicit examples.

6) Evaluation plan / metrics
- For extraction: field-level precision/recall F1, and % of JSON parse failures.
- For classification: accuracy, confusion matrix for top 3 classes.
- For summarization: ROUGE-L + human label for "adds new facts" (binary).
- Track tokens-per-inference and average latency for each template.

7) TODOs
- Curate 10 canonical examples per use-case with gold annotations (assign to Jordan).
- Write regression tests in prompt-regression-tests repo (PR skeleton exists in linked_artifacts).
- Add token count and cost estimate columns.
- Move final templates to confluence page and mark final versions.

References / links:
- Confluence prompt library (linked above)
- GH PR: prompt-regression-tests/pulls/12 for test harness prototype
- Slack: #devexp-prompt-library thread for discussion

Notes: keep entries terse. This doc will be iterated on heavily; keep original quick test snippets around for reproducibility.

Signed-off: Lee
